Sweep the Threshold of Remoteness of the Molecular Diagnostic Branch

Source: R/barcoding_threshold.R
sweep_barcoding_threshold.Rd

Step 9 of the branch. Without a rule of remoteness the nearest neighbour names a cactus species for any query: in the outgroup control, 288 of 312 outgroup queries came out in state 1. This step applies the rule (a query whose distance to its nearest neighbour exceeds a threshold is state 3, reason remoteness) over every threshold observed, and fixes an operating threshold per locus.

Usage

sweep_barcoding_threshold(
  classifier_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "7_classifier"),
  controls_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "8_controls"),
  output_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "9_threshold"),
  alignment = c("add", "library"),
  q = NULL,
  quantile_type = 1L,
  figures = TRUE,
  method = c("nn", "idtaxa"),
  species_q = 0.95
)

Arguments

classifier_dir

Character. Output directory of classify_barcoding_folds().

controls_dir

Character. Output directory of run_barcoding_controls(). When it holds no TABLE_barcoding_cn2_queries.csv the rejection is reported as not measured everywhere.

output_dir

Character. Destination; refused inside a directory of the phylogeny.

alignment

Character. Which predictions of step 7 are swept: "add", the default, reads the tables of alignment = "add", measured the way a user query is measured; "library" reads those of the joint alignment.

q

Numeric. Quantile of scheme G that sets the operating threshold. Defaults to 0.99 of the distances for "nn" and 0.01 of the genus confidences for "idtaxa".

quantile_type

Integer. Type of stats::quantile(). Defaults to 1L, whose result is always a distance observed in the data.

figures

Logical. Write one figure per locus, PDF and PNG at 300 dpi, 180 mm wide.

method

Character. "nn", the nearest neighbour and its rule of remoteness, or "idtaxa", IdTaxa and its confidence threshold. With "idtaxa" the tables read are TABLE_barcoding_predictions_<scheme>_idtaxa.csv and TABLE_barcoding_cn2_queries_idtaxa.csv, the curve runs over the confidence threshold, the operating threshold of a locus is the quantile q of genus_confidence of its scheme G queries (the rule of D1 turned around, since confidence rises where distance falls), and it is reported next to 60, DECIPHER's default, in the column rule. The tables written carry the suffix _idtaxa.

species_q

Numeric. With "idtaxa" only: the quantile of the species confidence of the scheme G queries of each locus (species absent from the library) that sets its species threshold, never under 60. Written to TABLE_barcoding_species_threshold_idtaxa.csv and read by the identification functions through threshold_dir; the validation (step 10) stays at 60. Defaults to 0.95.

Value

Invisibly, a list with curve and operating. Writes TABLE_barcoding_threshold_curve.csv, TABLE_barcoding_threshold_operating.csv and, with figures = TRUE, FIG_barcoding_threshold_<locus>.pdf and .png.

Details

For every locus and scheme the curve reports the legitimate queries in five disjoint outcomes (correct species, wrong species, correct genus, wrong genus, not assigned; a wrong species and an honest genus are never summed) and, when the outgroup control has comparable outgroup queries for the locus, how many of them the rule rejects. Outgroup queries that match the locus in neither direction are not comparable and stay out.

The operating threshold of a locus is the quantile q (type quantile_type of stats::quantile()) of the distances of the legitimate queries of scheme G: a cactus whose species is missing from the library while its genus is present, which is the query the rule must not reject. It is fixed without the outgroup queries, which then report the rejection with its exact binomial interval; a locus with no comparable outgroup query reports it as not measured.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sweep_barcoding_threshold(
  classifier_dir = "11_barcoding/7_classifier",
  controls_dir = "11_barcoding/8_controls",
  output_dir = "11_barcoding/9_threshold"
)
} # }
